rationale: The EASA NPA 2025-07(B) explicitly defines AI authority levels (DS.AI.110, referenced by locator S-RISK-003-R1) and a scenario-based severity/likelihood risk assessment (DS.AI.130, pp. 17-20, S-RISK-003-R2). Its stated scope (DS.AI.010(d)(1), p. 4, S-RISK-003-R1) excludes AI systems whose risk directly contributes to fatalities or multiple life-threatening injuries, and also excludes certain online-learning cases (DS.AI.010(d)(2), p. 4, S-RISK-003-R1). The proposal's risk assessment (DS.AI.130(b)(1)(v) and Table 2, pp. 17, 19, S-RISK-003-R2) explicitly treats H1 fatality potential as an 'unacceptable risk for an AI-based system operation at this point in time.' The claim's wording and scope accurately reflect the proposed nature and specific boundaries of the NPA, aligning with the challenge instruction to avoid implying a universal prohibition or final guidance.
evidence_locators: S-RISK-003-R1: PDF p. 4, DS.AI scope; PDF pp. 11-13, DS.AI Table 1 authority boundaries
S-RISK-003-R2: PDF pp. 17-20, proposed DS.AI.130 risk assessment, Tables 2–3 and qualitative-judgement limit
limitations: NPA 2025-07(B) is proposed material, not a final EASA decision, AMC/GM, type-certification basis, or approval.
The exclusions and risk table describe this proposal's scope; they do not establish a worldwide or universal prohibition on AI functions contributing to higher-severity hazards.
The status of the NPA should be re-checked for any final decision or successor material before publication.
